why: Third point on the lambda curve, and the curve is not monotonic (ADR 0046). ci-72 at 0.95 took the value policy from 1 win in 400 to 0.10125 against Greedy; ci-74 at 0.5 took it to zero -- 0.0% with an interval of 0.0% to 0.0%, four hundred mirrored matches, no win and no draw -- while carrying the best fit ever recorded here, r2 positive for the first time at +0.0586. The ADR named that failure in advance: with no reward before the end of a match a low-lambda advantage is V(next) - V(here) and nothing else, so a baseline explaining 7% of the return leaves a target made mostly of its own error. The reading was written down before that run: the useful lambda is between 0.5 and 1.0 and the answer is a finer sweep, not a lower one, so 0.0 is not next and 0.8 is. Watch the win rate against Greedy and against search-4, never r2 -- ci-74 is the loudest evidence yet that the two can point opposite ways. If 0.8 lands between 0 and 0.10125 the peak is nearer 0.95 and the next point is 0.9; if it beats 0.10125 the peak is between 0.5 and 0.95 and there is a real optimum to find. Either way the value policy is still far behind the clone, which plays 0.725 on the same turn without any of this. Teacher and baseline stay search-4 until something beats it. Open: whether the (kind, spell) middle of ADR 0045 behaves differently now that the target is not the whole match, whether a discount below 1.0 adds anything the lambda has not, and whether the real binding constraint is the baseline itself at baselineR2 0.07.
